keyFindings.description: This change switches every pod of Stage 4b to the SQL session store (`+    session_store: postgres` is an addition of this branch; main's rig named no store) and leaves every transcript reader in the harness reading a file inside the pod. `claim_session_text` (:1034-1038) takes the claim's recorded `sessionFile` and runs `pod_exec … cat --` on it; under `session_store: postgres` that path is the key of a row in `omp_session_files`, not a file on the pod (`internal/ompsessions/ompsessions.go:1-8`: the table "keys a session by the path its file would have had (the session file a claim records)"). The `cat` fails, `claim_session_text` returns non-zero, and every checkpoint built on it reads nothing: `planning_tasks` (:1043-1045), on which `child-reentered` waits (:3599-3600), plus `assistant_said` (:927), `session_contains` (:2146), the tree-2 planner session copy (:3745), the implementer's task read (:4193), the review-pair and transcript collection (:4415, :4491, :4525, :4585) and the subagent read (:4514), which cats a path derived from the same key. `pair_text`'s own read (:975) is the same shape. Stage 4b has run at no head, so nothing has met this. Every pod-session consumer needs one SQL-backed reader; the operator-launched controller's sessions are genuinely files and stay as they are.

The gap record narrows the round-2 window and does not close it. `held := r.strandedPod(name)` is taken before the confirming `readSandbox`, and the comment at :86-91 states the trade deliberately: taken first it misses the gap only if a whole foreground delete ran between the two, where taken after it would miss a Create landing between them. The first is the narrower window and the choice is right, but it is still reachable — the observer's GET can be delayed by seconds under API-server load or a throttle, which is the condition `evaluate` already answers with `Uncertain` elsewhere, and in that window the launch records the uid and completes the delete after the empty snapshot was taken. The verdict is then final and the incarnation is forgotten (`watch.go:130-131`), so nothing can repair it. Remedy in the function's own idiom: take a generation counter under `r.mu` beside `strandedPod`, read it again after `readSandbox`, and return `Uncertain` when it moved — the claim stays watched and is evaluated again. A race read from the code; not reproduced.

The contract census is stale at the head in the one number it exists to carry. `internal/api/version.go:330` is `const DaemonAPIVersion = 37`, with the collision note explaining that this branch took 36, main then landed INFRA-229 at 36, and the branch moved above it; both plugin manifests declare 37. The body still says `The daemon/plugin contract rises to 36` in the Change bullets, `Raised: the daemon/plugin contract, 35 → 36` in the census, and argues the rollout in terms of `a daemon before 36` and `an image built before 36`. The census is what tells an operator which image the release must carry, and the number is the whole of it. The version.go entry itself is correct and consistent.

Step 9 of the cutover this change writes is wrong twice in one sentence; found by the tester, routed to me by the architect. `kubectl -n legion get pvc -l legion.dev/project=<PROJECT>` with the upper-case placeholder selects nothing: the label's value is `claim.ProjectToken(cfg.Project)` (`internal/daemon/bootreads.go:41`), which `internal/claim/token.go:26` lower-cases and strips, while `legion.dev/issue` and `legion.dev/tree` carry the key unchanged (`names.go:271-277`), so the two label families genuinely differ and a blanket sweep would break the working commands. Second, the sentence that the command "answers this question with silence whether the cutover worked or not" is wrong with the correct value too: the controller's claim template carries `r.labels(l)` (`podkind.go:312-317`) and a repository cache's objects carry `labelProject` (`repocache.go:96`), so the selector returns those. The step's real instrument is the `jq` over every claim by owner that follows, which carries no selector and is unaffected — the fix is one placeholder and one clause.

The proof's contract disagrees with the proof again, in the same way round 2's three lifecycle rows did. The `pod-baseline` row still promises the stub agent's environment carries `OMP_SESSION_STORAGE=file`; this change makes the store mandatory SQL and `live_operator_test.go:180-183` now asserts `ompsessions.StorageVariable: ompsessions.SQLStorage` with the DSN pointer beside it. This table is where a maintainer looks a checkpoint up, so a wrong expected result here outlives the script.

`controllerPod`'s type comment still describes the init container this round deleted: "its one init container creates nothing on that volume, and refuses only a pod handed the provisioning token". `initContainers` returns nil at :335. The comment is the one place a reader learns what the controller's pod is made of.

testerCorrection.note: The tester corrected its own committed handoff over Envoy: `coverageInventory.provenWithoutACluster`'s second bullet said the round-1 claim was measured on the same storage class as an issue's disk, and it was not — the build namespace's own scratch class, at 20Gi, with volumeMode set explicitly where the daemon lets the API server default it, and 'about a second' is an upper bound from two polls rather than a timing. The pull request body carries the correction at the inventory bullet, which I read at this head; I take the body and that message over the committed sentence, and the conclusion is unchanged.
